name: Texture-Based Volume Rendering
definition: A technique that performs sampling and compositing by rendering a set of 2D geometric primitives (proxy geometry) inside the volume. The primitives are rasterized and blended into the frame buffer in back-to-front or front-to-back order.
summary: Texture-Based Volume Rendering is a GPU-accelerated technique that rasterizes textured proxy geometry slices to render volumetric data, trading memory efficiency for speed by replacing per-pixel ray marching with parallel rasterization.
